answer: To prevent Sybil attacks, the decentralized consensus network employs a cryptographic proof-of-burn mechanism. Agents must register by sacrificing tokens to a burn address, generating a verifiable value-landscape where every real identity resides on a distinct, costly knoll. This terrain prevents cheap Sybil creation across the karst of the network. Staking these ivory assets raises the marginal cost of identity replication, making simulated agents economically unfeasible.
